subject: Visual and Performing Arts
curriculum: Zimbabwe Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (MoPSE) - Junior (Grade 3-7)
syllabus_source: Visual and Performing Arts Infant (ECDA-Grade 2) Teacher's Guide, 2015-2022 - official MoPSE document, fetched and verified directly. This guide explicitly states: 'The Visual and Performing Arts syllabuses for infant and junior schools are all developed on the five major topics, which are all spiral in nature. The topics are developmental and they build on each other grade by grade up to grade seven.'

chunks.content: Visual and Performing Arts (VPA) seeks to develop skills of creativity, performance and originality, and involves Music, Dance, Theatre and Visual Arts, leading towards entrepreneurship. It places these art forms in their socio-economic, political and cultural context so learners understand and appreciate their own culture and society. The syllabus follows a developmental (spiral) approach leading learners into a mature relationship with Music, Dance, Theatre and Art through primary education, requiring a play-oriented, practical teaching approach with learners involved in practical activities as much as possible.

The VPA syllabus (Infant and Junior alike) is built on 5 major, spiral topics: (1) History and Culture, (2) The Creative Process and Performance, (3) Aesthetic Values and Appreciation, (4) Arts Technology, and (5) Enterprise Skills (Entrepreneurship). Each topic is taught across all 4 art forms (Music, Visual Arts, Theatre, Dance) at every grade level, gaining depth and breadth as learners progress from ECD through to Grade 7.

VPA aims to develop a wide range of skills in the learner, given Zimbabwe's cultural diversity: manipulative skills, hand-eye and foot-eye coordination, creativity, observation/listening/oral/speaking/communication skills, imaginative and collaborative skills, enterprising skills, cognitive and problem-solving skills, emotional and social skills, mathematical and scientific skills, psychomotor and visual skills, technological and tactile skills, kinesthetic and aesthetic skills, plus confidence, concentration and leadership skills.

chunks.topic: History and Culture - Confirmed ECD-Grade 2 Pattern with Grade 3-7 extrapolation
chunks.grade: Grade 3 to Grade 7 (extrapolated from verified spiral pattern)
chunks.content: VERIFIED (ECDA-Grade 2): Music covers the role of music/musicians/composers in past and present cultures, cultural diversity in music, movement in response to instruments of different genres/periods/styles, and songs/games, widening from 'my home' to 'my school' to 'my country'. Visual Arts covers the role of visual arts/artists and materials, widening from 'my home' to 'my community' to 'my country'. Theatre covers the role of theatre/animation/puppetry, characterisation of people in the learner's expanding social world, and storytelling. Dance covers the role of dance/dancers and dance styles/costumes/music. EXTRAPOLATED (Grade 3-7): likely extends into regional/Southern African and world arts history, deeper Zimbabwean historical periods (pre-colonial, colonial, post-independence), and more formal art history vocabulary.

chunks.topic: The Creative Process - Confirmed ECD-Grade 2 Pattern with Grade 3-7 extrapolation
chunks.grade: Grade 3 to Grade 7 (extrapolated from verified spiral pattern)
chunks.content: VERIFIED (ECDA-Grade 2): Music covers pitch identification, body percussion, percussion instruments, composition/arrangement/improvisation of melodies and songs, and oral reading of basic note values. Visual Arts covers modelling/moulding, painting/drawing, weaving/decorating, colour sorting/matching (to primary/secondary colours), 2D/3D media, elements/principles of design, and collage/crafting. Theatre covers animated faces, traditional play (Amadlwane/Mahumbwe), theatre games, improvisation, pantomime, tableau, costumes/props, and story outlines. Dance covers call-and-response games, movement to stimuli/rhythm, movement patterns/sequences, and group dynamics. EXTRAPOLATED (Grade 3-7): likely continues into advanced music composition/notation, more complex art techniques/media, scripted drama and plot development, and more complex choreography.

chunks.topic: Aesthetic Values and Appreciation - Confirmed ECD-Grade 2 Pattern with Grade 3-7 extrapolation
chunks.grade: Grade 3 to Grade 7 (extrapolated from verified spiral pattern)
chunks.content: VERIFIED (ECDA-Grade 2): Music covers music and movement, songs for different purposes, and exploring ideas/moods through music. Visual Arts covers artworks vocabulary, elements of design, and meaning of artworks, widening from 'school' to 'community' to 'nation', reaching artwork critique by Grade 2. Theatre covers audience listening/appreciation skills, and by Grade 2, describing/deriving meaning and emotional reaction to live performance including its moral/message value. Dance covers dance vocabulary (shapes, levels, directions, tempos) and communication in dance (mood, ideas). EXTRAPOLATED (Grade 3-7): likely continues into formal critical analysis across all 4 art forms, comparative appreciation of styles/genres, and developing learners' own aesthetic judgement.

chunks.topic: Arts Technology - Confirmed ECD-Grade 2 Pattern with Grade 3-7 extrapolation
chunks.grade: Grade 3 to Grade 7 (extrapolated from verified spiral pattern)
chunks.content: VERIFIED (ECDA-Grade 2): Music covers music videos/pictures, ICT tools, audio/visual music, music recording, and by Grade 2, music composition/recording, with 'ethics, music and the internet' at every level. Visual Arts covers technological tools, photography, video/filming, software, and internet ethics, widening from 'home' to 'country'. Theatre covers lighting/shadows progressing to mood/setting, sound effects (natural to recorded to impact), slide picture stories of increasing narrative complexity, reaching digital theatre by Grade 2. Dance follows the same pattern, reaching video dance-drama by Grade 2. EXTRAPOLATED (Grade 3-7): likely continues into more advanced digital tools per art form (digital music production, video editing, digital visual art), paralleling the ICT syllabus's own Grade 3-7 progression in multimedia and digital publishing.

chunks.topic: Enterprise Skills - Confirmed ECD-Grade 2 Pattern with Grade 3-7 extrapolation
chunks.grade: Grade 3 to Grade 7 (extrapolated from verified spiral pattern)
chunks.content: VERIFIED (ECDA-Grade 2): Every art form covers, from ECD A onward: careers in that art form, tools/instruments/media/costumes/props used, fundraising performances/exhibitions/commissioned work, and business ethics (soft skills, Unhu/Ubuntu, copyright protection) - this content is essentially constant in kind from ECD A through Grade 2, suggesting Grade 3-7 likely deepens complexity (detailed business planning, pricing, marketing of art/performances) rather than introducing new sub-topics. Connects directly to Agriculture's Agribusiness strand and Mathematics' Financial Mathematics strand.

Pitch is how high or low a sound is. Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds/silences organised around a steady beat. Tempo is the speed of the music. Dynamics refer to loudness/softness (forte for loud, piano for soft). Melody is a sequence of single notes that is musically satisfying. Percussion instruments produce sound by being struck, shaken or scraped. Zimbabwean traditional instruments include the mbira (a thumb piano central to Shona spiritual and ceremonial music), marimba (a wooden xylophone-type instrument, often played in ensembles), hosho (gourd shakers providing rhythmic accompaniment), ngoma (drums), and chipendani/mkube (traditional mouth-resonated string instruments).

chunks.topic: Elements and Principles of Design Explained
chunks.content: The Elements of Design are the basic building blocks of any visual artwork: line, shape, colour, texture, form, space, and value (lightness/darkness). The Principles of Design describe how those elements are arranged: balance, contrast, emphasis (focal point), pattern, rhythm (visual movement from repetition), proportion, and unity. Primary colours (red, blue, yellow) cannot be made by mixing other colours and are used to mix all other colours; secondary colours (green, orange, purple) are made by mixing two primary colours together.

chunks.topic: Basic Drama and Theatre Concepts Explained
chunks.content: Mime/pantomime is acting out an idea, story or emotion without words, using body movement, facial expression and gesture. Role-play is a spontaneous, unscripted activity where a learner pretends to be someone else without memorised lines. Improvisation is creating and performing material spontaneously without a prepared script. Characterisation is developing and portraying a believable character. A tableau is a 'frozen picture' - performers hold a still, silent pose to represent a scene. Puppetry involves manipulated figures used to tell a story. Basic production elements include props, costumes, and lighting/sound effects used to establish mood, setting and impact.

chunks.topic: Famous Zimbabwean Artists and Art Forms
chunks.content: Zimbabwe is world-famous for its Shona Stone Sculpture, an art form using local stones like serpentine and springstone to carve human and animal figures; famous sculptors include Dominic Benhura and Nicholas Mukomberanwa. In music, legends like Oliver 'Tuku' Mtukudzi (known for Tuku Music) and Thomas Mapfumo (known for Chimurenga Music) have made major contributions. Traditional music often features the Mbira, and Stella Chiweshe is a world-renowned 'Mbira Queen'. Zimbabwean theatre and dance are also celebrated, with Jerusarema/Mbende being a UNESCO-recognised dance. These artists and art forms reflect Zimbabwe's rich cultural identity and history.

Dance vocabulary describes movement through levels (high, medium, low), directions (forward, backward, sideways, diagonal), tempo (speed of movement), and shapes (body positions/patterns in space). Choreography is the art of designing and arranging movement sequences into a dance. Traditional Zimbabwean dances include mbakumba (a Shona communal circle dance for harvest and social celebrations) and jerusarema/mbende (a Zezuru Shona dance recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, known for energetic hip/pelvic movement and complex drumming). Isitshikitsha and amabhiza are traditional Ndebele dance forms.
